shapes.text: Premier League models and their trading strategies.

Collected and checked team and player data.
Built models for home wins, draws and away wins.
Tested betting rules and recorded profits, losses and risk.
Produced money-progression graphs and timestamped forecasts.
Only completed work is shown. Historical backtests are not verified real-money trading results.
Sources: study_status.json | Full paths in notes
2025/26: the common season available for every strategy. Every line starts at 100,000.
Each line is one model + betting rule + stake size. The following model statistics use the full four-year evaluation.
Sources: graph_equity_2025_all.csv | Full paths in notes

Stake means the amount requested for one bet. The next pages state the setting for every strategy.

Amount varies with estimated advantage and odds; the listed % is a ceiling
A 2% cap means at most 2,000 when cash is 100,000

Kelly example: 100,000 cash, a 40% chance and odds of 3.
Quarter Kelly requests 2,500; a 2% cap reduces the bet to 2,000.
Kelly stake = opening cash × min(cap, Kelly fraction × (probability × odds − 1) / (odds − 1)).
All bets on a date share opening cash. Date caps apply to their combined stakes. Reduce all requests proportionally when needed; never borrow.
